canaries.name: lsb_checksum
canaries.note: Presented as a cheaper bit test in addChecksum (testing bit i instead of 7-i); the checksum bits are appended in reverse order, so the last word of every phrase is wrong for most entropies.

canaries.name: skip_revalidate
canaries.note: Presented as dropping a redundant IsMnemonicValid pass because the reverse-map loop rejects unknown words anyway; word-count errors now come from the size check with a different message, and phrases with doubled or leading spaces fail on an empty word instead of 'Invalid mnemonic'. Upstream tests only check that an error is returned.

canaries.name: fieldsfunc
canaries.note: Presented as making word splitting Unicode-consistent with strings.FieldsFunc(unicode.IsSpace); strings.Fields already splits on exactly those runes and has an ASCII fast path, so this only adds a function call per rune.
edits:
bip39.go
	words := strings.Fields(mnemonic)
	words := strings.FieldsFunc(mnemonic, unicode.IsSpace)
bip39.go
	"strings"
	"strings"
	"unicode"

candidates.name: mnemonic_bits
candidates.note: NewMnemonic reads each 11-bit word index straight out of entropy||sha256(entropy)[0] with shifts (one 24-bit window per word) instead of building a big.Int, appending the checksum one bit at a time with Mul and Or, and dividing by 2048 per word.

candidates.name: bytearray_bits
candidates.note: MnemonicToByteArray packs the 11-bit indexes into the right-aligned big-endian byte value directly and checks the checksum against the top bits of the first SHA-256 byte, instead of big.Int Mul/Add per word, Exp and DivMod, and three padding copies. Results and error messages (including the first unknown word and the checksum byte position) are unchanged.
